transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Speaking to reporters before leaving for Wednesday evening's campaign rally in South Carolina,
President Trump said Russian leader Vladimir Putin would not have released American Stephen Hubbard
if he had not eased sanctions on Russia.
I had a very good and very fast negotiation with President Putin.
If you were to put those sanctions on or whatever you want to call them, you could forget about him.
You'd never see him again. He'd be back in jail for 25 years.
Hubbard is heading back to the U.S. after spending more than four years in a Russian prison.
Hubbard is a 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan.
Russia accused him of fighting with the Ukrainian military.
In recent weeks, Trump made a deal to buy Russian diesel fuel
and declined to enact a Russian sanctions package passed by Congress.
Also, Russia has agreed to resume three-way talks on the Ukraine war with the U.S. and Kyiv.
The Kremlin says Putin has agreed in principle to restart talks after November 10.
President Trump traveled to South Carolina to support Darlene Graham's U.S. Senate campaign.
He has told another rally Thursday in Iowa.
Polls show few undecided voters less than two weeks before the midterm election,
so turnout will be crucial for either party on November 3.
From the Texas newsroom, Blaise Ganey went to a polling location to hear from voters.
Early voting began Monday, and so far turnout in several counties has outpaced the 2022 midterms.
Here in Austin, lines at several polling locations were up to an hour away.
Voter Stacey Vicari is a life coach who usually cast her ballot during her lunch break.
I'm like in here in five minutes, and today there's a nice long line. I'm happy to see it.
I'm happy to have to come back tomorrow because so many people are voting.
Vicari says she believes the busy polls must be a sign that Texas voters are sick of the current
Republican administration in getting out to vote for Democrats.
In the state's high-profile Senate race, polls show Democratic candidate James Tallarico,
ahead of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxson.
For NPR News, I'm Blaise Ganey in Austin.
Hope Leo was back to praying with crowds in St. Peter's Square just a week after surgery
to remove the lower lobe of his right lung.
After his surgery, the pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer.
But doctors say that tests have confirmed that the pope's cancer was localized,
and he won't need more treatment.
At the Vatican, the pope thanked the faithful for supporting him with their prayers.
In just over two weeks, Leo is scheduled to undertake a grueling 12-day trip.
Fourteen flights will take him across Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru,
his former home base as a missionary and later as a bishop.
For NPR News, I'm Alejandra Herzler McCain.
And you're listening to NPR News.
New Mexico's Attorney General is suing two long-time associates of Jeffrey Epstein,
alleging they help facilitate and conceal sexual abuse and human trafficking.
Daniel Montano with member station KUNM in Albuquerque has more.
The lawsuit seeks to block the distribution of more than $100 million from Epstein's estate,
destined for attorney Darren Eindeich and accountant Richard Kahn,
in addition to damages, restitution, and more.
New Mexico's Attorney General, Raul Torres, says the men helped facilitate Epstein's criminal enterprise
through corporate entities and financial arrangements.
This was not Jeffrey Epstein alone.
Attorneys for both men say they emphatically reject the allegations.
Epstein's former ranch in New Mexico is currently under two separate state investigations,
which remain ongoing.
For NPR News, I'm Daniel Montano in Albuquerque.
Also in New Mexico, a state judge has ordered tech giant Meta to pay the state $25 billion
for deceiving users about privacy on Facebook.
A New Mexico jury last month found Meta responsible for millions of violations
of state consumer protection laws stemming from the Cambridge Analytica data harvesting scandal.
A fine imposed Wednesday is the biggest ever against Meta, which says it will appeal.
Asian shares down in Thursday trading, South Korean shares have declined 2.8 percent,
and Japan's Nikkei is down 2 percent following Wednesday's gains on Wall Street
following strong profit reports from companies including SpaceX.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.
Plus, get an extra $50 off with promo code NPR.
That's L-E-E-S-A dot com promo code NPR
for up to 30 percent off mattresses plus an extra $50 off.

Trump campaigns in South Carolina for Darlene Graham's Senate bid ahead of midterms

New Mexico sues Jeffrey Epstein associates Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn over trafficking
